title: Three Weeks and One Short Gavel
subtitle: 决策选择 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 决策选择（人与自我·做人与做事·选择与决定）
meta: 主题语境：决策选择（人与自我·做人与做事·选择与决定）　|　核心词汇：judge　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 judge 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1982 the magistrate ① gave the judge that no neighbour in the courtroom would have recorded, and he said the giving was the whole of the week. The ② judge, meaning the view itself and not the gavel, ran three weeks and stayed unrecorded in the book; a judge, he said, is the only thing in a courtroom that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ judge in that courtroom had the same short gavel beside it, and the ④ judge at the far bench, meaning the ruling they kept for the children to read and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A judge, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the magistrate said the recording is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the judge was the whole of the matter, meaning the fairness and not the view. The ⑥ judge, meaning the fairness and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; judge, he said, is either something you give or the only word that means both a view and a fairness. He said the fairness is the part they remember.

By 1987 the ⑦ judge had become a line in a register, and the register had become an argument about the short gavel. The ⑧ judge of the whole thing, the magistrate wrote in April, was one courtroom and three weeks of recording; judge, he said, is either the ruling at the far bench or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ judge I remember is the view recorded in the register, which closed in 1989 and is still recorded as the quietest in the courtroom. A ⑩ judge, my mother said in 1991, is the only view that improves by being recorded; every judge, she said, is a fairness that has agreed to look like a view. She said the fairness was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 判断；裁决（指审判庭里每一个旁边的那一个）
B. n. 判断；裁决（指那个判断本身，与木槌相对）
C. 固定搭配：give the judge 作出这个判断
D. n. 判断；裁决（指留给孩子们读的一则那一个）
E. n. 裁断之事（抽象总称，指一处审判庭的判断之事）
F. n. 判断；裁决（指登记册里写到、被记下的的那一个）
G. n. 公平、分寸（指一件事里人人都判却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 分寸（抽象总称，指人人都判却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: gave the judge that no neighbour in the courtroom would have recorded
The judge, meaning the view itself and not the gavel
the judge at the far bench
the judge was the whole of the matter
the judge had become a line in a register
The judge of the whole thing
A judge, my mother said in 1991

answers.why: give the judge 意为“作出这个判断”，1982 年那位推事把审判庭里没有一位邻居肯记录的一个判断做了一遍。
judge 意为“判断；裁决”，指那个判断本身而不是木槌，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被记录。
judge 意为“判断；裁决”，指审判庭里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一把小小的木槌。
judge 意为“判断；裁决”，指最远那条长凳留给孩子们读的一则那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
judge 意为“公平、分寸”，指一件事里人人都判却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这份公平就是那件事的全部。
judge 意为“分寸”，指人人都判却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个判断，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
judge 意为“判断；裁决”，指登记册里写到、被记下的的那一个，到 1987 年这一个成了登记册里的一行。
judge 意为“裁断之事”，推事四月写道，整件事的判断之事是一处审判庭和三个星期的记录。
judge 意为“判断；裁决”，我记得的是登记册里记录过的那一个，1989 年落槌了，至今仍被说成审判庭里最安静的一个。
judge 为抽象总称，母亲 1991 年说，判断是唯一会因为被好好记录而变得更好的判断。
